messages:
Evelyn (Research): Heads up 3-day research trip to Cape Town starting 2026-08-10. I'll be working remotely during the days there for a partner study. Questions: 1) Do I get WFH stipend while traveling internationally? 2) Should this be submitted as travel expense instead? 3) Any company tax/PE or export control issues for doing IRL research and calls from ZA?
Jordan (People Ops): Good Q. Short answers: 1) WFH stipend can apply for short international stays but its normally prorated by days in-month; if travel is business-funded (project budget) we prefer expense route not stipend. 2) Submit a travel request for project-funded trips: https://redwood.internal/travel-request and check the project PO for expense coverage. 3) For international remote work or research >30 days we loop Legal. For short stays under ~30 days it's usually fine, but we still need a record.
Ravi (Payroll): For payroll/tax: personal income tax residency is personal and varies by country. Company-level permanent establishment (PE) risk is low for single short visits, but any sustained work or formal business presence could change that. Please mark the days on the travel request and select "working while abroad" so Payroll can flag for review. Also note: the WFH stipend is paid in USD and may be taxed locally depending on local rules, but that's employee-level.
Saanvi (Benefits): Benefits remain active for short international travel. Check international telehealth access and out-of-country prescriptions. If you plan to access local healthcare in ZA, DM me and well confirm coverage or advise on pay-and-claim.
Evelyn (Research): This is partially project-funded (the team will cover accomodations) but I also want the monthly WFH stipend for the days I keep regular remote hours. Can I do both?
Marcus (Legal): Quick legal note: dual funding ok but we prefer to avoid duplicative payments for the same expense. From PE and export-compliance POV: if youre only doing meetings/calls and research interviews it's low risk. If youre shipping hardware or transferring controlled data to local collaborators, stop and escalate. For stays >30 days we need a short memo describing activities so Legal can sign off.
Jordan (People Ops): Actionable: Evelyn, please submit a travel request and check "working while abroad". In the form choose "partial project-funded" and indicate stipend request. We'll evaluate and confirm whether stipend or expense reimbursement applies. Travel link: https://redwood.internal/travel-request
travel-bot: Travel request received (TR-5802). Status: pending approval from manager and People Ops. Please attach project PO if available.
Ravi (Payroll): After travel approval, Payroll will determine if stipend payout should be prorated or paid as expense. If you elect stipend, check the box for "temporary international stipend" so our tax vendor can assess withholding exposure.
Evelyn (Research): Done 580-2 submitted and checked working-abroad + temp-stipend. Attached PO referencing project funds. Thanks all.
Jordan (People Ops): Got it. We'll review with Legal + Payroll. If approved, stipend = prorated days in-country (days worked) and any project-covered travel costs billed to PO. Marcus will confirm if we need the memo for >30 days.
Marcus (Legal): Noted. If this extends beyond 30 days or you start co-locating with a partner organization, ping Legal immediately and we'll request the activity memo.
Evelyn (Research): Appreciate it. I'll keep the trip under 30 days and escalate if plans change. Thanks!
